close_reason: Bad-premise. Verified: canonical jmap-mail-client uses the exact same tests/helpers.rs + #[path = "helpers.rs"] mod helpers; idiom (mail-client/tests/mailbox_smoke_tests.rs:14, search_snippet_smoke_tests.rs:16, submission_*.rs, etc., across 7 integration test files all sharing one helpers.rs). All 6 other extension-client siblings (chat, calendars, tasks, contacts, filenode, mail) use the same shape; only sharing-client uses tests/common/. So metadata-client's tests/helpers.rs is canonical-correct, not divergent. The bead's premise that 'canonical sibling jmap-mail-client has tests/common/' is factually wrong. The defensive concern (future contributor forgets the #[path] line) is real-ish, but converting metadata-client alone to tests/common/ would create a fresh divergence from canonical — which is the inverse of the propagation rule. If the workspace decides tests/common/ is preferable, that should land canonical-first via a workspace-wide propagation bead. Closing as no-op for this crate.
description: tests/helpers.rs declares two pub fns (make_session, make_client) but is included into only one integration test file (tests/metadata_tests.rs) via '#[path = "helpers.rs"] mod helpers;'. The canonical sibling jmap-mail-client has tests/common/ with multiple integration files using the same harness — that's the shape the cookie-cutter assumes. Today this works, but the moment a second tests/*_tests.rs file lands and forgets the #[path = …] line, the second file silently has no harness; rustc cannot warn because tests/helpers.rs is a separate top-level integration target (running '0 tests'). Trigger: future contributor adds tests/metadata_set_tests.rs without copying the #[path] declaration; CI passes; the new tests do not in fact use the shared harness. Fix: convert to the canonical 'tests/common/mod.rs' layout used by mail-client (it forces the same #[path] = "common/mod.rs" idiom that's easier to spot). Low cost; gets it right before there's a second integration file.
title: tests/helpers.rs: only-used-from-one-file path hack tolerates dead_code only by accident
